decisions.issues: Clean. Nagoji matches the ch19 Ananthan Pillai row: topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold stud, plain white mundu and shoulder cloth, heavy silver chain of office with a medallion, ivory-handled knife at the waist. He sits on the stone platform under the jackfruit tree, with kalari sparring beyond the wall and dark monsoon cloud building. Minor: the pale scar lines are on the top of the left forearm, not clearly the inner side, but they read as pale ridges with no emblem or letters. Both captions fit in the clear cloudy sky at upper right (x 0.55 to 0.85, y 0.02 to 0.25) or over the roof tiles at upper left.

The setting, Padmini (grey threading in coiled black hair, walking stick, simple gold) and the bundle hand-off all work. The candidate fails because Nagoji's LEFT forearm, which rests on his knee outer side to camera, carries a dark circular stamped emblem with a glyph-like shape inside. That reads as a tattoo or symbol, not the bible's pale puckered ridged brand on the inner forearm. There is also an extra long white scar on his upper arm, and the chain of office is a thin necklace instead of panel 1.1's heavy silver chain with a medallion. Smaller deviations: Padmini hands the bundle into his palm instead of tossing it into his lap, and Nagoji fills half the frame instead of sitting at its edge.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, setting, light and both figures exactly as they are: Padmini standing at left under the jackfruit tree with her walking stick, grey threading through her coiled black hair, holding out the small cloth-wrapped bundle; Nagoji seated on the stone platform at right with his Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, plain white mundu with no gold border, shoulder cloth and the ivory-handled conch-marked knife at his waist. Change only these. His LEFT forearm rests on his knee with the outer side toward camera, and that outer forearm shows NO mark of any kind: no dark circle, no stamped emblem, no tattoo, no symbol or glyph. The old brand sits on the inner side of the left forearm, turned away from camera, and at most its edge shows as a pale puckered patch of raised ridges. No scar on his upper arm or biceps; the only scar is the long thin white line on the inner left forearm. His silver chain of office is the same heavy silver link chain with a round silver medallion as in panel 1.1, not a thin necklace. Keep the clear cloudy sky and the leaves at the top as open space for one speech balloon.

Padmini looks back over her shoulder, walking stick in hand, in the same jackfruit courtyard, with the kalari and the wet paving matching 1.1 and 1.2. The grey in her hair is much fainter than in 1.2, and her face is harder and a little younger than in 1.2, though close to her sheet. Both balloons fit in the open grey sky above and to the right of her head (x 0.2 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.17).

This is not the ch19 Nagoji, and it is not the scripted close-up. His hair hangs fully loose, with no Kerala topknot and no grey at the temples. There is no silver chain of office, no shoulder cloth and no conch knife. The long white scar is on his RIGHT forearm (the viewer's left), and the left wrist with the brand is not shown. decisions.correction: Frame this as a true close-up on the hands. Crop from mid-chest down to the knees so Nagoji's head is OUT of frame, with no face and no hair. At the top of the frame show the heavy silver link chain of office with its round silver medallion on his bare chest, the plain cream shoulder cloth over one shoulder, the plain white mundu with no gold border across his lap, and the ivory-handled knife with the conch mark at the mundu's waist fold. Both hands sit in the centre of the frame, unwrapping the coarse grey-brown cloth bundle, the fingers slightly unsteady; the fingernails are visibly ridged and discoloured. His LEFT hand is on the viewer's right, turned so the inner left wrist and forearm face up toward the viewer. The old brand there is a pale puckered patch of raised ridges with no letters, numerals, symbols or cross, and a long thin white scar runs from it toward the elbow. His RIGHT forearm has no scar. Keep the fine grey-black dust sifting from the folds onto the white mundu, as now. Keep the courtyard behind soft and low-detail (wet paving, a glimpse of the jackfruit trunk, monsoon cloud), and leave the shaded chest and shoulder-cloth area plus the background in the top third clear for two caption boxes.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. A folded sheet of paper, not palm leaf, opens in both hands, with sound anatomy. Minor issues: (1) the ink marks are dense pseudo-cursive in a Latin-looking hand, illegible as the script requires but closer to a European letter than to Marathi Modi script; (2) the top of the head is cropped, so the topknot is not visible, and the hair at his visible temple shows no grey; (3) it is an over-the-shoulder view rather than a tight insert. Captions fit in the cloudy sky at upper right (x 0.62 to 0.85, y 0.0 to 0.2) or over the plain shoulder cloth at lower left (x 0.0 to 0.4, y 0.55 to 0.95), clear of his face and hands.

Minor: there are three small riders with a saffron swallow-tailed pennant in the left middle ground that the script does not call for. Minor prop changes: the father carries a rope-lashed wooden pick rather than a plough (a plough appears behind the oxen in the background). Minor: the two bands are closing head-on rather than shown mid-pass, and the blue sky is a little cooler than the warm dry letter palette. Otherwise the panel matches 2.3. A walled hill fort stands on a cliffed scarp, and two bands of riders in white angarkhas and pagdis face each other on the dusty road. One band rides under a saffron swallow-tailed pennant and the other under a plain dark red pennant, with no emblems or lettering. The riders eye each other with hands near their hilts. Horse and rider anatomy holds up, and the torn-paper edge is there. Open sky at top left and top right gives room for the two captions.

Minor only: the silver chain of office is not visible on the exposed chest (the 3.1 lock does not require it, but the chapter row does); a light stubble shadow on the chin still reads as clean-shaven; a fair amount of loose hair hangs below the topknot. Wet eyes, gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, smeared unreadable ink on the paper, and the jackfruit courtyard with kalari boys all match the script and page 1. Caption space: the cloudy sky at top right (x 0.6 to 0.95, y 0.0 to 0.25).

Nagoji is drawn twice. decisions.correction: Only ONE human figure in this panel: Nagoji as Ananthan Pillai, seen from BEHIND at the right edge of the frame and cropped to the back of his head, neck and one shoulder (Kerala topknot high on the crown with the first grey at the temples, a plain white shoulder cloth over a bare shoulder, the small gold ear stud just visible; no face shown, no captivity rags, no loose hanging hair). Behind and beside his head, the Chapter 3 storm bleeds in like a spreading ink stain with ragged, dissolving edges, filling most of the panel, with only scraps of jackfruit leaves and red-tile roof surviving at the outer edges: black water boiling around the dark wooden hull of the ship, the deck heeled steeply, and one thick rope stretched taut across the wet planks toward a flooded square hatch, with no people on deck. Keep the upper-left quarter as dark, low-detail storm sky or spray, with no text or boxes, so two captions can sit there.

decisions.issues: Minor: the hairline graze is drawn with a reddish tint. It reads as a scrape, not running blood, but it is close to the no-blood rule. The wave rises around him rather than clearly over his head. Fill the top fifth of the frame with plain, out-of-focus white mundu cloth or grey stone as clear, low-detail space for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor: two sardars wear red pagdis, and the cross-legged one with folded arms also has a red waist cloth. Clean. The beat is right: an afternoon courtyard with dappled shade, Nagoji tucking a blank folded letter into his mundu waist, Padmini a few steps off leaning on her stick, women carrying brass pots and boys in the kalari behind. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch19 row: greying topknot, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, silver chain, plain mundu and shoulder cloth, the ivory knife with the conch mark, and the long pale scar on his left forearm. There is no text in the art, and the hands are sound. The staging is good: Padmini stands close with her stick planted, looking down, and Nagoji sits on the stone platform under the jackfruit tree, looking up. The problem is the brand on his LEFT forearm, which sits mid-frame beside his clasped hands. It is drawn as a crisp dark circular stamp with a cross-like bar and glyph strokes inside. That reads as a seal, logo or tattoo, and arguably as pseudo-text. The bible requires a pale, puckered patch of raised ridges, blurred past reading, and explicitly not a cross. It also sits on the outer mid-forearm, not the inner forearm above the wrist. Minor: Padmini has a small red dot on her forehead that is not on her sheet.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition and lighting exactly: bright afternoon in the same inner courtyard, Padmini standing at frame left in her cream sari with the gold border, stick planted, looking down at him, and Nagoji seated at frame right on the worn stone platform under the jackfruit tree, looking up at her, forearms resting on his knees, with small kalari boys sparring in the background. Fix his arms. Draw NO circular stamp, seal, ring, emblem, tattoo, symbol, cross or letter-like shape anywhere on either arm. If the old Portuguese brand shows at all, it is only a small, pale, puckered patch of irregular raised ridges with soft blurred edges, on the INNER side of his LEFT forearm a hand's width above the wrist, the same pale tone as the long white scar and never dark or outlined. It is better to turn that inner forearm down toward his knee so only the long pale scar is visible. Padmini has no forehead mark. Keep the sky and foliage across the top third low-detail and clear of both heads, so there is room for four speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor notes. Padmini is alone, in the same bright courtyard as 4.1 and 4.2. Her face, stick, cream-and-gold sari and gold jewellery match the sheet. Lettering space: open sky at top centre for the balloon and low-detail paving at lower right or the canopy at top right for the caption.

Acceptable, with one art note. Clean enough to use. Acceptable. Varma alone in the same room (brass lamp, red bolster, shelves of palm-leaf bundles and plain-spined volumes, doorway to the pillared corridor at right). He wears the sheet's court look and has a faint smile, looking right toward Nagoji, who is off panel. Hands are clasped and sound, and there is no text. The prop is wrong. The letter is drawn as a thick stack of pages tied with cords, like a bound palm-leaf or paper book. decisions.correction: The letter is the same single sheet of cream paper Varma held in the previous panel: one thin folded sheet with soft fold creases, lying flat on his knee over the cream cloth with the broad gold border, its lower edge toward the camera. It is NOT a palm-leaf bundle, NOT a bound book or ledger, NOT a stack of pages, and has no cords, covers or binding. His right forefinger, with the gold ring and red stone on it, taps one line close to the bottom edge of the sheet. The handwriting is faint rows of ink marks only, nothing readable. Keep the rest as it is: the tight insert of his bare arm with the gold bangle and armlet, the pearl and gold necklaces at the top edge, the brass oil lamp at right, the shelves of palm-leaf bundles and the dark pillared doorway behind, and clear low-detail wall and shadow in the upper part of the frame for two balloons.

decisions.correction: Draw the brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm as a pale, slightly raised, puckered patch of healed ridges, lighter than the surrounding skin and blurred past reading, beside the long thin white scar. Do NOT use dark ink, tattoo lines, glyphs or any letter-like or numeral-like shapes. At the left edge, show only the dark wooden front of the same low platform with the red bolster as in the neighbouring panels, cropped below its seat so it does not read as an empty seat. Keep everything else unchanged: Nagoji cross-legged on the woven mat, eyes lowered, right hand at his chin, black topknot with only first grey at the temple, tiny gold ear stud, silver chain, ivory conch-marked knife, plain white mundu and shoulder cloth, the brass oil lamp, the shelves and the dark pillared doorway at right, and the plain laterite wall at upper centre left clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: The key beat is missing, and there is a stray silhouette. The script's point is that the lamp behind the king throws his shadow across the mat and over Nagoji. Here the lamp stands between the two men, Nagoji is fully lit, and no shadow reaches the mat. Instead, a large head-and-shoulders shadow sits on the back wall to the right of the lamp. With the lamp there, that is physically impossible as the king's shadow, and it reads as a third, unseen figure in the room. Everything else works: Varma at left leaning forward with an open hand, stern, in full court dress; Nagoji at right on the mat, matching his sheet (clean chin, stud, topknot, chain, knife, brand with no letters); sound hands and feet; the same room and doorway.
decisions.correction: Put the single brass oil lamp behind the king, at the far left on the platform behind his back, so it backlights him. His long dark shadow falls forward to the right, across the woven floor mat, and climbs over Nagoji's crossed legs and chest, leaving Nagoji's lower body and part of his face in the king's shadow. Paint no shadow silhouette on the back wall and no shadow of anyone but the king. Keep everything else unchanged: Varma on the low wooden platform with the red bolster at left, leaning forward with his open hand extended toward Nagoji, stern, in the court turban with the peacock crest, pearl earrings, forehead mark, necklaces and gold armlets; Nagoji cross-legged on the mat at right, looking up at him, with topknot, clean-shaven chin, tiny gold stud, silver chain and ivory knife; the shelves, the rolled maps, and the dark pillared doorway at right. Keep the upper wall between the two men plain and low-detail for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Low angle with the lamp in the foreground, one Deccan fort stain with cannon behind his head, Ananthan look correct (topknot, temple grey, bare-headed, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain, conch knife, clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud). Reject. The panel shows two Nagojis and no king. On the king's platform, seen from behind, is a grey-topknotted Ananthan figure with the silver chain, the conch knife and the forearm scar. His head is turned toward frame-left and tilted slightly up to meet the eyes of the king, who sits on a higher platform just off the left edge. decisions.issues: Reject. The brand on the forearm is drawn as a crisp, letter-like glyph (it reads like 'ψP') on the outer forearm, which is pseudo-text and against the bible (blurred ridges, no letters, inner left forearm). decisions.issues: Acceptable and matches the script. The bible says explicitly that it is not a cross. The two foreground Nair officers wear their hair in back or crown knots instead of front knots. decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition: the view from the dark pillared corridor through the open doorway, two bare-chested Nair officers in shadow in the foreground at left and right edges, Varma reclining on his red-cushioned platform with a faint half-smile flicking one hand, and Nagoji half-risen from the mat in the same lamp-lit laterite room with brass lamp and wall map as the previous panel. Fix Nagoji's LEFT forearm: on the inner forearm a hand's width above the wrist there is only a pale, puckered patch of raised ridges blurred past reading, and beside it one long, thin white scar running in a single line from the wrist toward the elbow. There must be no cross, no plus sign, no X and no crossing or intersecting lines anywhere on the arm; if this cannot be guaranteed, turn the forearm away from camera or keep it in shadow. Give both Nair officers their hair in a short knot at the FRONT of the head above the forehead, all black with no grey and no ear studs, white mundu hitched to the knee, no shoulder cloth and no chain, so neither can be mistaken for Nagoji from behind. The shelves hold only palm-leaf manuscript bundles and cloth-wrapped boxes, with no European leather-bound books.

decisions.issues: The two foreground Nair officers are drawn as copies of Nagoji: long curly black hair, a thick curled moustache, a small gold ear stud, a cream tunic and a rust-red sash (Nagoji's own commander look). Readers would see three Nagojis in the panel. They also fail the script and break continuity with 7.2, where the same two officers are bare-chested in white mundu with a front hair knot, no shoulder cloth and no sash. The mark on Nagoji's left forearm is an arc on top of a vertical line that reads like an anchor or cross, not a puckered patch beside a straight scar. Padmini's hair hangs loose and shows none of the grey threading the bible requires from chapter 16. The fort yard, bullock carts, gatehouse, daylight, and Nagoji and Padmini walking in the midground all work, and there is ample sky for the lettering.
decisions.correction: Keep the sunlit laterite fort yard, the tiled gatehouse, the bullock carts being loaded with sacks and pots, and Nagoji (greying Kerala topknot, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain of office, plain cream mundu with shoulder cloth, ivory conch-marked knife at the waist) walking in the midground beside Padmini with her stick. Replace the two foreground men completely. They are the SAME two Nair officers as in the previous corridor panel: bare-chested, white mundu hitched to the knee, black hair tied in a short knot at the FRONT of the head above the forehead, curved Nair swords at the hip. They wear no tunic, no shoulder cloth, no red or rust sash, no chain and no ear studs. Their faces must be clearly unlike Nagoji's: no long curly shoulder-length hair and no thick curled moustache. Make one younger and clean-shaven and the other heavier-jawed with a thin moustache, both turning their heads to follow Nagoji as he passes. On Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm show only a pale, puckered patch of raised ridges a hand's width above the wrist and one long, thin straight white scar from wrist toward elbow beside it, with no cross, anchor, arc or crossing lines. Padmini's thick black hair is coiled at the nape, with grey threads through it.

decisions.issues: Minor only. A faint vertical line on Nagoji's right upper arm could be read as a second scar; it is subtle. His chin carries light stubble shading. He matches the bible row: greying topknot, moustache, gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu with shoulder cloth, conch knife, and on the inner left forearm the puckered ridged brand with the white scar beside it (not a cross). Padmini matches her sheet: grey-threaded black hair gathered at the nape, gold necklace and earrings, a cream sari with a gold border in the old drape with no blouse, and her stick. Hands are sound. The carts roll out through the same gate and yard, which suits a redone 7.3. The sky at top centre and the plain laterite wall at left give room for both balloons in reading order: Nagoji high at top centre, Padmini lower left.

Minor only. The beat reads well: evening verandah, carved pillars, lamps lit, Revathi with arms folded facing Nagoji. Both match their sheets. Nagoji has his topknot, grey at the temples, gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, silver chain, white mundu with shoulder cloth, and the conch-marked knife. The brand on his LEFT forearm is drawn as a dark circular spiral near the elbow, not a pale puckered patch above the wrist. It has no letters and is not a cross. Revathi has a thin red streak in her hair parting where her sheet shows an ochre line. No painted text. The sky between the left pillars (upper left, above and right of Revathi's head) is clear room for both of her balloons.

Minor only. This is a tighter two-shot in the same verandah and light as 8.1: Nagoji's mouth is tight and Revathi's chin is raised. The scar and faint brand marks sit correctly on his LEFT forearm (the arm on screen right, with the shoulder cloth over his left shoulder). His chain carries a round engraved silver medallion that 8.1 does not show (it may be hidden under the cloth there). No visible sandalwood line at Revathi's hairline. Her arms are folded with her hands tucked in, which is fine. No painted text. Room for balloons is tight but workable: the roof and sky above and between the two heads, Nagoji's upper left of centre and Revathi's upper right.

Minor only. Revathi leans on a carved pillar, smiling with a playful look down at Nagoji's chest. She matches her sheet: sandalwood line, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets. Nagoji is now seated on the verandah floor, though he stood in 8.1 and 8.2; the script does not forbid it, and it justifies her looking down. His chain is drawn with heavier links and a round pendant, chunkier than in 8.1 and 8.2. The scar and brand are on his LEFT forearm (screen right). The knife is at his waist. His hands and Revathi's hands are sound. No painted text. The open evening sky at top centre and the roof at upper right hold both Revathi lines clear of both faces.

The close-up works well otherwise: lamplit verandah, topknot at the crown, grey at the temples, gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, and a half-smile that does not reach his eyes. But the silver chain of office is missing. His bare neck, collarbone and upper chest are fully visible, so the chain would have to show. It vanishes in the panel straight after Revathi's line about the chain, and the bible row for chapters 18-19 requires it. There is also some stubble shading on the chin and jaw.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, lighting and expression: a close-up of Nagoji on the lamplit evening verandah of the Velinadu house, beside a carved dark-wood pillar, with brass lamps behind. Keep the Kerala topknot high on his crown, grey at the temples, small gold ear stud, thick curled black moustache, and the half-smile on his mouth that has left his eyes. Keep the white shoulder cloth draped over his LEFT shoulder. Add his silver chain of office, clearly visible around his neck: a plain silver chain of medium links, the same chain as the other panels on this page. It lies across the bare collarbone and upper chest on the uncovered side, hangs toward the sternum, and passes under the shoulder cloth on the other side. Show no engraving or letters on any pendant. Keep the chin and jaw smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble shading.

decisions.issues: The setting is right: night, a full moon over coconut palms, moonlit water channels between the trees, Nagoji alone on the laterite steps at the edge of his quarters' verandah, white mundu, fine silver chain, sound hands and feet. But his hair hangs loose to his shoulders with no topknot and no grey at the temples. The script for 8.5 and the bible row both require the Kerala topknot high on the crown with first grey at the temples, as in 8.1 to 8.4. His ear stud also reads pale and pearl-like rather than gold, and his jaw has noticeable stubble.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition exactly: a wide night scene with a full moon in the upper right sky, coconut palms, irrigation channels and flooded field strips glinting with moonlight between the trees, and Nagoji sitting alone on the red laterite steps at the edge of the small verandah of his quarters, beside a wooden post, with a single oil lamp burning in a wall niche behind him. Keep his pose (forearms resting on his raised knees, looking up and out), the plain white mundu with shoulder cloth, and the fine silver chain. Fix his hair: gather his long curly black hair into a Kerala topknot tied high on the crown of his head, with only a few loose curls at the nape. Show clear streaks of grey at both temples, matching the earlier panels of this page; his hair must not hang loose over his shoulders. Make the small ear stud plainly gold. Keep the chin and jaw clean-shaven and smooth under the thick curled moustache, with no stubble shading. Keep the upper sky around the moon clear and low-detail for two captions.

decisions.issues: v01 does not match Nagoji's ch19 bible row or script 9.1. His hair is loose curls with no Kerala topknot and no grey at the temples. The silver chain of office is missing. He wears a long-sleeved white shirt and a red shoulder cloth, which breaks continuity with 8.5 (bare-chested, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, chain). The ridged brand is on the forearm at image left, which is his RIGHT arm because he faces the viewer. The bible puts it on the inner LEFT forearm. The framing is a waist-up shot with his face, not the 'close on his hands' the script asks for. What works: sound hands, ridged discoloured nails, faint rope lines on the palms, the moonlit verandah with the niche lamp, and the clear sky at upper right.
decisions.correction: Frame this as a true close-up: the two hands and forearms held out palms up fill the centre of the frame, with Nagoji's bare chest, the silver chain of office and a cream shoulder cloth behind them, cropped at the chin or showing only the moustache and lower face at the top edge. If any of his head shows, his hair is gathered in a Kerala topknot high on the crown with only the first grey at the temples, never loose curls. He wears no shirt, tunic or sleeves: bare arms, a plain cream mundu and a cream (not red) shoulder cloth, matching the previous panel. The pale ridged brand (raised puckered ridges, no letters, not a cross or symbol) and the long thin white scar sit on the inner LEFT forearm just above the wrist. With his palms up and facing the viewer, that is the forearm on the IMAGE RIGHT, and the forearm on the image left is unmarked. Keep what worked: the ridged, discoloured nails, the faint healed rope lines across both palms, sound five-fingered hands, cool moonlight on the hands, the brass lamp in the wall niche burning low, the moonlit palms and glinting channels beyond the verandah, and clear sky at upper right for the caption.

decisions.issues: v01 breaks the beat: Keshavrao (who drowned in ch3) sits on the present-day verandah as a full figure in rags and manacles next to Nagoji. The script calls for only his thin manacled hand at the hatch frame inside the memory stain. The panel also drops 'the same hands' foreground from 9.1. Nagoji's hair is heavily grey, beyond 'first grey at the temples'. His brand is drawn as a spiral or conch-like symbol rather than puckered ridges. The memory vignette itself (bandaged, manacled hands on a rope, the storm and the hatch) is close to what the script wants.
decisions.correction: Keshavrao must not appear as a figure on the verandah or anywhere in the present. He is dead and exists only inside the memory stain, where nothing of him shows except his thin manacled hand and wrist gripping the edge of the hatch frame at the far end of the rope (no face, no body). Compose the panel as a continuation of 9.1. In the foreground are Nagoji's present-day hands held out palms up: bare forearms, ridged discoloured nails, faint rope lines on the palms, and the pale ridged brand with a long white scar on the inner LEFT forearm (image right), drawn as puckered raised ridges, never a spiral, conch or any symbol. Behind and around those hands, the Chapter 3 storm bleeds in like a dark watercolour stain over the moonlit verandah: his younger, captivity-era hands bandaged in cloth and locked in iron manacles joined by a short chain, gripping a rope that frays and tears through the bandage cloth, the rope running back through rain and waves to the hatch frame and Keshavrao's hand. Rain and waves stay inside the stain, and the verandah itself is dry. If Nagoji's head shows at all, he has a Kerala topknot with only the first grey at the temples, not a head of grey hair. No blood. Keep clear dark sky or stain area across the top for three captions.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor points. The script beat is met: three hands-only insets show the father's old thick-knuckled hands on a plough handle (with a dark kambal at the edge), the mother's turmeric-stained hands in green glass bangles rolling a stone roller on a grinding stone at dawn, and the brother's ink-stained fingers at a tied angarkha cuff drawing a single line with a reed pen by a brass open-wick lamp. There are no faces and no pseudo-text on the paper or book bundles. Minor: the plough beam in inset 1 does not visibly connect to the distant yoked oxen. Insets 2 and 3 start below a pale top band while inset 1 runs to the top edge, but that band and the dawn sky over insets 1 and 2 give clean space for the three captions.

Clean. It shows a thin moonlit surface line at the top, black water below, a wrecked hull, broken timbers, a split spar with loosely wrapped rope (not a noose) and loose planks settling on the sand. No bones, no body, no figure, no text. The large empty dark water from about 15 to 45 percent of the height holds both captions without covering anything.

v01 matches the action, setting and costume. He stands, reaching into the wall niche beside the door to turn up the brass lamp's wick, with warm light on his face. He wears a white mundu and shoulder cloth, the silver chain and the ivory conch-marked knife, and the moon sits lower over the palms. But his hair is loose shoulder-length curls with no Kerala topknot and no grey at the temples. That contradicts both the bible row for ch18-19 and script 9.5 ('topknot greying at the temples'). Note for the orchestrator: the existing 8.5 frame has the same loose-hair error, so 8.5 may need the same fix for page-to-page consistency.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's hair must be gathered into a Kerala topknot high on the crown, black with only the first streaks of grey at the temples, never loose curls falling to the shoulders. Keep his face, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and small gold ear stud exactly as drawn. Keep everything else that worked: he stands on the verandah reaching into the wall niche beside the door to turn up the wick of the small brass open-wick oil lamp, the flame climbing and throwing warm light across his face. He is bare-chested in the plain white mundu with the cream shoulder cloth, the silver chain of office and the ivory-handled conch-marked knife at the waist. The moon sits lower over the palms and glinting channels at left, and the sky and roof shadow at upper left stay clear for the two captions.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate) gets the beat right: harbour market, a stall under an awning, the sowcar cross-legged with scale, ledger, inkpot and reed pen, and Nagoji (topknot greying at the temples, shoulder cloth, mundu, silver chain, conch knife) setting the pouch down. It also leaves clear sky upper left for lettering. Rejected for Nagoji's brand. The forearm reaching for the pouch is his RIGHT arm, the one on his bare near shoulder. It carries a short reddish scar and a crisp wheel or rosette emblem on its outer surface. The bible puts the brand and the long white scar only on the INNER LEFT forearm, as a pale puckered patch blurred past reading. A crisp emblem on the wrong arm breaks a plot-critical mark. Smaller points: his ear stud reads pale or pearl rather than gold. The sowcar's red turban is large rather than a small pagdi. With a thick moustache, clean chin and ear stud, the sowcar also looks too much like Nagoji, and he does not match the bearded sowcar of 10.2.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, market, morning light and the clear sky upper left exactly. Nagoji kneels at left: Kerala topknot greying at the temples, bare chest with the cream shoulder cloth over his left shoulder, plain white mundu, silver chain and the ivory conch-marked knife. He sets the leather pouch down on the white-cloth platform. The sowcar sits cross-legged at right with the balance scale, cloth-bound ledger, brass inkpot and reed pen. FIX: Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, the one reaching for the pouch, is completely unmarked. No scar, wheel, rosette, stamp, tattoo or emblem of any kind on it, on his hands or on his upper arms. His brand and long white scar exist only on the INNER side of his LEFT forearm. Keep that left arm down at his side with the inner forearm turned away from the viewer, so neither shows in this panel. Give him a tiny flush GOLD ear stud on the lobe. The sowcar must not resemble Nagoji: a fleshier, older face, a short neatly trimmed black beard with a moustache, and no ear ornament. He wears a SMALL close-wound red pagdi, not a large round turban, and a white angarkha tied at the side.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate) has the right setting and cast. The sowcar weighs the pouch on his palm with eyebrows raised. Nagoji in profile has the topknot, grey temples, gold stud, clean chin, chain, shoulder cloth and conch knife. The sealed letter with red wax lies on the white cloth, and the awning and sky leave room for four balloons. Rejected for two reasons. (1) The brand: Nagoji's near LEFT forearm hangs with the back of the hand to camera. It shows a crisp sun-face emblem near the elbow on the OUTER forearm, with the scar on the outer face too. The bible wants a pale, shapeless, puckered patch on the INNER forearm a hand's width above the wrist, blurred past reading. A crisp emblem reads as a tattoo or sigil. (2) The beat: the sowcar's index finger points at the scale foot and the coin tray, not at the sealed letter, which lies well to the left by the inkpot. That weakens his line 'And this?'. Minor: his red turban is large rather than a small pagdi, and he is bearded here but clean-chinned in 10.1.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, market, awning and morning light. The sowcar sits cross-legged at left on the white-cloth platform, weighing the leather pouch on his raised palm with eyebrows lifted, the balance scale and brass inkpot in front of him. Nagoji sits at right in profile: Kerala topknot greying at the temples, tiny gold ear stud, cream shoulder cloth, plain white mundu, silver chain and the conch-marked ivory knife. Keep the awning and sky above the two men clear for four balloons. FIX 1: lay the folded letter with its red wax seal on the white cloth directly beside the foot of the scale. The sowcar's extended index finger points straight down at that letter, fingertip just above the seal, never at the scale or the coins. FIX 2: Nagoji's forearms carry no emblem, sun, face, rosette, stamp or tattoo anywhere. His brand is only a pale, shapeless, puckered patch of raised scar ridges on the INNER side of his LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, with the long thin white scar beside it. In this pose rest his left forearm inner side down against his thigh so neither brand nor scar is visible. Leave his outer forearms and the backs of his hands plain skin. Keep the sowcar's short trimmed black beard and moustache, with no ear ornament. Make his red pagdi small and close-wound, and his white angarkha tied at the side.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate) has the right mood: warm, dim night palette, a low wooden board on a woven mat, wavy unreadable ink lines, a brass inkpot, and a dark wall above the lamp with room for captions. Rejected because Nagoji is drawn in the wrong look. His long curly hair hangs loose over his shoulders, with no Kerala topknot and no grey at the temples. He wears a stitched cream tunic with a red sash, which is the ch16 to 17 commander look, and a talwar leans in the room. There is no silver chain and no shoulder cloth. The bible row for ch18 to 19 requires Ananthan Pillai: topknot, mundu and shoulder cloth, chain of office. The framing is a three-quarter front view, not the scripted over-the-shoulder shot. The lamp burns a candle stub in its bowl; the setting bans candles and calls for an open wick. Its stand-lamp shape also differs from the spouted pedestal lamp in 10.4.
decisions.correction: Keep the warm, dim lamplit night palette, the laterite wall, the woven mat and the low wooden writing board. Keep the sheet of wavy, unreadable ink lines, the small brass inkpot, and the clear dark wall above the lamp for the three captions. FIX: this is Ananthan Pillai, not the commander. His long curly black hair is gathered into a Kerala topknot high on the crown, with the first grey at the temples and no loose hair over his shoulders. He is bare-chested, with a cream shoulder cloth over one shoulder, a plain cream mundu and the silver chain of office round his neck. No stitched shirt or tunic, no red sash, and no talwar or sword anywhere in the room. Frame it OVER HIS RIGHT SHOULDER, from behind and slightly above. In the near foreground: the back of his head with the topknot, his shoulder, and the edge of his ear with its tiny flush gold stud. His face shows at most as a lost profile. The focus is the board, the paper and his RIGHT hand moving a plain cut reed pen; that right forearm is unmarked. The lamp is a small brass oil lamp with an open cotton wick burning at the spout of its oil bowl, with a tall bright flame, never a candle or candle stub. Match the brass pedestal bowl lamp with a spout in panel 10.4, set beside the board.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. A tight insert: the hand moves a reed pen along wavy ink lines (no letters or pseudo-text), and the page is about half filled. The brass spouted pedestal lamp with an open wick and the brass inkpot sit on the low board on a woven mat, against a laterite wall, in lower, redder light as scripted. The dark upper wall gives ample space for the one caption. Hand anatomy is sound. Minor: the ink-darkened pen tip reads slightly like a metal nib. The rendering is more painterly than the inked panels, but it matches the 11.1 insert. The cream cloth at the wrist could pass for the shoulder cloth.

Fails the script beat and continuity with 10.4. The script wants 'the same sheet, finished', but the sheet is blank paper with only one squiggle line along the bottom edge. In 10.4 the same page was already half filled with lines, so here the letter looks erased instead of completed. The pen across the inkpot (it has a dark, metal-looking nib) and the small bead-like lamp flame are right. The rendering is photographic rather than inked comic art.
decisions.correction: The sheet on the low writing board must be the same letter as in the previous panel, now completely filled: even rows of short wavy ink strokes (abstract marks only, no letters, no script, no numerals) running from the top margin all the way down the page, with the last row shorter and ending near the bottom edge. No large blank area of paper may remain, only the margins. Keep the rest: the dark laterite wall above as empty space for two captions, the woven mat, the low wooden writing board, the reed pen laid across the round brass inkpot, and the small brass oil lamp beside it whose flame has shrunk to a tiny bead. The pen is a plain cut bamboo reed (kalam) with a cut reed tip, not a metal nib. Draw it in the same inked comic-illustration style as the market and gate panels of this chapter, not photographic.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The sowcar's forearm is bare under a draped white cloth instead of a long white angarkha sleeve, and there is a dark green cloth at the right edge. He is a one-chapter non-principal, and the lettering identifies the hand. The stall, scale, ledger, brass inkpot, red wax and folded hundi match 10.1 and 10.2, and there is no text in the art. There is open sky across the top for both balloons.

Acceptable, with minor deviations. Nagoji stands in the gateway itself, so he reads less clearly as arriving along the path. Padmini looks at his face rather than down at his empty hands, though his hands are visibly empty. Her grey threading is faint. Nagoji's jaw has slight stubble shading, but the chin reads as clean. Everything else matches: topknot greying at the temples, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, brand and scar on the left forearm, gold ear stud, the sunset gold light, the lamp in the tharavadu, and the jackfruit tree for 12.6. For lettering, the caption and Padmini's balloon fit in the sunset sky at top left, and Nagoji's short 'Yes.' fits on the dark gate beam above his head.

Nagoji is off-model for chapters 18-19 and does not match 11.3. His hair is long, loose and curly with no topknot and no grey at the temples. There is no silver chain of office on his chest; a chain hangs at his waist from the knife instead. The composition is good: over Padmini's grey-threaded coiled hair onto Nagoji, with him glancing back down the road toward the market traffic, in sunset light, with the gate behind him.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's hair must match the previous panel and his chapter 18-19 look: his long curly black hair is gathered into a Kerala topknot tied high on the crown, with clear grey streaks at the temples. No loose hair falls over his neck or shoulders. The silver chain of office hangs around his neck on his bare chest, as in the wide gate shot. There is no chain at his waist and none hanging from the knife. Keep everything else: the over-the-shoulder view from behind Padmini (grey-threaded black hair coiled at the nape, cream sari with gold border, walking stick in her hand); Nagoji in plain white mundu and shoulder cloth with the ivory-handled knife at his waist; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; his glance back over his shoulder toward the road on the right where carts and walkers recede toward the market; the laterite gate with its lamps and the red-tiled tharavadu behind; and the low gold sunset light. Leave the sky at upper right as clear space for two balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 does not show the script beat. 12.1 is a TIGHT insert on the hand closing on the chain, but this is a medium shot that includes the full face. In that face Nagoji has long loose curly hair with no Kerala topknot and no grey at the temples, which breaks the ch18-19 bible row. The chain is a heavy one with large medallion discs, unlike the plain silver link chain in 12.2 and 12.6. The brand is a dark spiral symbol on the outer forearm, not the pale puckered patch on the inner LEFT forearm. The palm scars are not visible because only the back of the hand shows.
decisions.correction: Frame this as a true TIGHT insert. Only Nagoji's LEFT hand and the patch of bare chest under it fill the frame, cropped below the chin so that no face, hair or ear is visible. His left hand lifts the plain silver chain of office slightly away from his chest, fingers curling around it, ridged fingernails pressed against the cold metal. The chain is a simple silver link chain matching the one in the neighbouring panels, with no medallion discs. The wrist is turned so the inner forearm and part of the palm face the viewer. Faint pale scars show across the palm and the heel of the hand. On the INNER LEFT forearm, just above the wrist, draw the old brand as a pale puckered patch of raised ridges blurred past reading: no spiral, no symbol, no letters, no numerals, not a cross. The long thin white scar runs from the wrist toward the elbow beside it. Show the edge of the plain white mundu and shoulder cloth at the frame's edges, with warm low dusk light raking from one side. Leave a soft, low-detail band of shadowed cloth or skin along the top of the frame for the caption.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. Padmini shows more than her shoulder and stick (the back of her head and her arm are in view), but her face stays hidden at the left edge, so the beat still reads. The brand on his left forearm is a small dark spiral rather than a pale puckered patch. There is light shading texture on his chin. The split background works: dusty Deccan on the left, palms, pepper vines and surf on the right, with no animals or figures. The topknot is greying at the temples, the ear stud and the silver chain are present, and the wind lifts his shoulder cloth. The two captions can go in the upper sky band and over the dark Deccan ground at upper left.

In v01 the silver chain of office is missing from his bare neck and chest. The bible row requires it, and 12.1, 12.2 and 12.6 all show it. He faces and speaks toward frame RIGHT, but Padmini is to the left in 12.2 and looks right toward him in 12.4, so the eyeline breaks the 180-degree line. The framing is a medium shot with a raised gesturing hand, not a close on the face. There is visible stubble texture on the chin and jaw, which the clean-shaven-chin rule does not allow outside captivity.
decisions.correction: Make it a true close-up: Nagoji's head and the top of his shoulders only, with no raised hand in the frame. He faces toward the LEFT of the frame in three-quarter view, speaking level and calm to Padmini, who stands off-panel to the left. Keep the Kerala topknot high on the crown with grey at the temples, the thick curled black moustache, the small gold ear stud and the white shoulder cloth. Paint the chin and jaw smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble texture. The plain silver link chain of office lies clearly visible across his bare collarbones and upper chest, matching 12.2 and 12.6. Keep the same background, softly out of focus behind him: laterite gate pillars with lit lamp niches, the red-tiled gate roof, the jackfruit tree and the dusk sky. Leave clear, low-detail space (dusky sky or the plain laterite wall) in front of his face on the left and above his head for one speech balloon and two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. The framing is fairly wide for a half-width panel, so crop toward Padmini on the left to keep the smile readable. Her far earring reads as a small hoop. The character match is good: grey threading in black hair coiled at the nape, cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape, gold necklace, stick, and a warm smile breaking her usual stern look. She looks right, toward Nagoji, which matches 12.2. The setting is the same gate at dusk with lamps in the niches. The caption and her balloon fit in the sky at upper left and on the laterite wall at left.

None. Padmini is seen from behind turning toward the gate, her hand on the stick. A narrow palm-leaf ola bundle is tucked at her waistband, tied with red thread, one end smoke-darkened, with nothing written on it. It is the same gate, courtyard and lamp niche at dusk. The caption fits in the open sky at upper right.

The scar is on the wrong arm. Nagoji is seen from behind, so the arm on frame right is his RIGHT arm, and it carries a long white scar crossed by a ladder of tally or cross marks. The bible locks the brand and the long thin white scar to the inner LEFT forearm only, and the brand must not read as crosses.
